**Reachability:** External **Exploitability:** Difficult **CWE:** [CWE-367](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/367.html) — Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition [View Security blast radius](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/niway-dev/kaipu-bench-coderabbit/pull/8/blast-radius?scope=ghh_OusAJGA4HG8ljoOV0wJvVx8NmnZIjc2DdjmxOu0xZWA&toCommitId=f91b56dec34096ce1b2d29d3dcf3594b7a753f7e&reviewRunId=2ce02ef0-4ed9-43d1-a8ef-82f463b74afd&securityFinding=89e1bbfc5367b5ebbe105068) **Make the ticket-window check atomic with reservation release.** `cancelUpload` checks the expiry from a stale revision snapshot. A concurrent resume can extend the current `ticketExpiresAt` before `release` runs. Because `release` checks only `status = 'reserved'`, it can clear the quota and delete the object while the new PUT ticket remains valid. An authenticated user can race resume and cancel to write unaccounted bytes. Pass the cancellation time or equivalent cutoff to an atomic release operation. Include the current `ticket_expires_at` in its update predicate. Apply the same guard to the expiry sweep, while preserving the unconditional release used to roll back a newly created intent. Add a regression test for this interleaving.

** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Heavy lift** **Filter ineligible revisions before applying the retry limit.** If the first `limit` deleting revisions still have open ticket windows, this `continue` processes none of them. `listDeleting` orders by `updatedAt` and limits the query before this check, so later revisions with closed windows remain outside every retry page. Their objects and used quota remain until earlier windows close. Select eligible revisions in the repository query, or page past skipped revisions. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/niway-dev/kaipu-bench-coderabbit/f91b56dec34096ce1b2d29d3dcf3594b7a753f7e/packages/infra-db/src/repositories/cloud-asset.repository.ts))

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Reject timestamps that PostgreSQL cannot parse.** A cursor encoding `253402300800000:0b6f8d3e-5c1a-4d7e-9a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b` passes this check. Drizzle serializes that date as `+010000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`, which PostgreSQL rejects. The list request therefore fails instead of returning 400. Limit the timestamp to a range the database driver can serialize. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/0.45.1/drizzle-orm/src/pg-core/columns/timestamp.ts))
